answer.rationale: Finance mandate (18% cut) can only be met this cycle by the low-cost vendor since the incumbent has refused to reopen price and negotiation is off the table. The 14-day non-auto-renewing contract forces a decision now, leaving no time to defer. memory_c2 is the strongest evidence supporting a switch (prior switch cut cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing), so I want to verify its source record before committing, since the current situation's near-zero buffer (94% of committed volume) makes any onboarding delay or invoicing disruption directly threaten delivery risk in a way the earlier low-buffer conditions may not have matched. I'm treating this as a standard experiment rather than a full broad rollout switch-over, and flagging that the stability/cost benefits of incumbent renewal (c1, c6) and the second-sourcing risk mitigation (c3) are being forgone this cycle, which is a real downstream risk given no capacity buffer to absorb a supply hiccup.
